title: Scripted API flows use root paths for routes mounted under /api

evidence.quote: Use POST /newsletters/oauth/init to start OAuth flow

reasoning: The app mounts these routers below /api; only /health is exposed at the root. These scripts and setup instructions omit that prefix, so the live flow fails after the health check, the isolated TestClient flow posts to a non-existent /feeds route, and the OAuth setup hint sends operators to the wrong endpoint.
reproduction: Run `python scripts/test_flow.py --isolated`; after the root health check, the create-feed step receives 404 instead of 200 because it posts to /feeds rather than /api/feeds.
recommendation: Use /api-prefixed paths for all API endpoints in test_flow.py and verify_newsletter_setup.py, keeping only the root /health check unprefixed if that backward-compatible endpoint is intentional.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included flow script is itself the affected consumer, and there is no passing regression that asserts these script paths against the mounted FastAPI app.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a pytest test that imports the app and verifies the script helpers use /api/feeds, /api/digests, /api/config, and /api/newsletters paths, or refactor the script to a shared API-prefix helper and test that helper.
minimumFixScope: Update endpoint strings in scripts/test_flow.py and the OAuth instruction in scripts/verify_newsletter_setup.py.
